name: NVIDIA H100 NVL
memory_bandwidth_basis: HBM3 5,225Mbps x 6016-bit = 3,938 GB/s. The product brief Table 2 gives memory clock 2,619 MHz (= 5,238 Mbps effective data rate), 6,016-bit bus, peak 3,938 GB/s - all three are stated, so this is a derivation, not an estimate.
notes: CRITICAL: datasheet prints 835 TF32 / 1,671 BF16+FP16 / 3,341 FP8+INT8 for H100 NVL, all WITH SPARITY; dense is half. Memory spec is fully primary-sourced (nv-h100-nvl-product-brief Table 2). CONFLICT on vram: the current NVIDIA product page (nv-h100-datasheet) says H100 NVL has 94GB, but the H100 NVL column there is a PER-CARD figure while the datasheet's own H100 NVL column is a 2x-paired aggregate (188GB, 7.8TB/s) - the datasheet footnote says specs for H100 NVL are 'shown for 2x H100 NVL PCIe cards paired with NVLink Bridge'. 94GB per card is the correct per-accelerator number and is what this record uses. tdp_w 400 is the >400W default from the product brief; the product page says 350-400W configurable. Notably this 94GB card has MORE bandwidth (3,938 GB/s) than the 80GB HBM3 SXM (3,350) while computing LESS. The 'other' row is FP64 30 TFLOPS (dense) - this schema's precision enum has no fp64 member.
